coverageNote: Seven items cover regular-polygon diagonals, joined regular polygons, polygon angle sums, supplementary interior and exterior angles, and a reflex angle at the centre of a regular polygon.

Halved $144$ instead of halving $180-144$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC=144^{\circ}$ (interior angle of a regular decagon)
$AB=BC$, so $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles
$x=(180^{\circ}-144^{\circ})\div2$

Used a hexagon interior angle of $120^{\circ}$ instead of the octagon's $135^{\circ}$.
Gave the octagon's exterior angle instead of the gap at the point.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle$ of a regular octagon $=135^{\circ}$
$\angle$ of a square $=90^{\circ}$
$x=360^{\circ}-135^{\circ}-90^{\circ}$
$=135^{\circ}$ (angles at a point)

questions.question_text: A pentagon has interior angles $90^{\circ}$, $108^{\circ}$, $97^{\circ}$, $x^{\circ}$ and $x^{\circ}$. Find $x$.

options.why: Found the sum of the two unknown angles but did not divide by $2$.
Used the quadrilateral angle sum $360^{\circ}$ instead of the pentagon angle sum $540^{\circ}$.
Divided the sum of the known angles, $295^{\circ}$, by $2$ instead of subtracting it from $540^{\circ}$ first.

questions.question_text: In convex pentagon $ABCDE$, the exterior angles at $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are $80^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$, $100^{\circ}$ and $70^{\circ}$. Find the interior angle $x$ at $E$.

options.why: Found the exterior angle at $E$ but did not subtract it from $180^{\circ}$.
Used $540^{\circ}$ as the exterior angle sum and returned the resulting exterior angle.
Added the four given exterior angles and used that total as the interior angle at $E$.

questions.solution_text:
$80^{\circ}+45^{\circ}+100^{\circ}+70^{\circ}+E=360^{\circ}$ (exterior angle sum)
$295^{\circ}+E=360^{\circ}$
$E=65^{\circ}$
$x=180^{\circ}-65^{\circ}=115^{\circ}$ (interior and exterior angles are supplementary)

questions.question_text: A concave pentagon has four interior angles of $90^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$, $40^{\circ}$ and $105^{\circ}$. Find its reflex interior angle $x$.

options.why: Subtracted the required reflex angle from $360^{\circ}$ and gave the smaller angle outside the polygon.
Used the quadrilateral angle sum $360^{\circ}$ instead of the pentagon angle sum $540^{\circ}$.
Added the four known interior angles but did not subtract their sum from $540^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: A regular dodecagon has centre $O$. Two adjacent vertices are $A$ and $B$. Find the reflex angle $AOB$.

options.why: Gave the smaller central angle $360^{\circ}\div12$ instead of the reflex angle.
Gave an interior angle of the regular dodecagon instead of the reflex angle at its centre.
Subtracted the polygon's interior angle $150^{\circ}$ from $360^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting the central angle $30^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle AOB=360^{\circ}\div12=30^{\circ}$ (equal angles at the centre of a regular dodecagon)
$r+30^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$ (angles at a point)
$r=330^{\circ}$

options.why: Gave $\angle ABC$ instead of continuing to find $\angle BAC$.
Copied the exterior angle as the answer.
Subtracted only $\angle BCA=47^{\circ}$ from $180^{\circ}$ and omitted $\angle ABC=62^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC=180^{\circ}-118^{\circ}=62^{\circ}$ (angles on the straight line $ABD$)
$x=180^{\circ}-62^{\circ}-47^{\circ}$
$=71^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)
